suno.role: Song generator that creates a full song, with vocals, lyrics and melody, from a text description.
suno.audience: Creators, students and hobbyist musicians who want songs or background music without production knowledge.
suno.status: Active. Per the v6 launch post, Suno will retire previous models and move entirely to the v6 generation.
pros: 50 free credits a day: the free plan gives 50 credits a day and uses the v6-mini model.
Ownership and commercial use on paid plans: per the help center, a song made while on a Pro or Premier subscription belongs to the user, and commercial-use rights persist after the subscription ends.

v6 model family built with record labels: v6 and v6-wild came out 9 Sep 2026 for Pro and Premier subscribers, developed per Suno with Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe. Added free-language section editing, mashups and samples.
cons: No downloads or commercial rights on free: the pricing page says 'No monthly song downloads' and 'No commercial rights' on Free. Per the help center Suno keeps ownership of free-generated songs.
Monthly download quota even on paid plans: Pro allows 20 song downloads a month, Premier 60 and Platinum 120. Unused credits don't accumulate.
Content is used to train models: per the privacy policy Suno may train its models on content users upload and create, and no opt-out is described.
suno.price: Pro is 96 USD/year (8 USD/month billed annually). Free plan with 50 credits a day, no downloads and no commercial rights.
suno.free: Free with no time limit: 50 credits a day and the v6-mini model. No monthly song downloads and no commercial rights; Suno keeps ownership of the songs.
plans: 50 credits/day, v6-mini model.
2,500 credits/month, 20 song downloads/month, v6 and v6-wild models, commercial rights.
Same as monthly Pro.
10,000 credits/month, 60 song downloads/month, v6 and v6-wild models, commercial rights.
Same as monthly Premier.
15,000 credits/month plus 20,000 visual credits, 120 song downloads/month, commercial rights.
Same as monthly Platinum.
suno.privacy: Per the privacy policy (last changed 23 June 2026), Suno may use content users upload and create, their activity and conversations 'to train and enhance the models that power our Services'. Voice recordings for the Voices feature are also used for training. The policy describes no opt-out and doesn't distinguish the free plan from paid plans.
suno.rights: Per the help center (edited 7 Jan 2026), a song made while on a Pro or Premier subscription belongs to the user, and commercial-use rights persist after the subscription ends. Songs from the free plan are owned by Suno.

elevenlabs.role: Platform for text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing and creating sound effects and music.
elevenlabs.audience: Content creators, students and developers who need narration, dubbing or synthetic voice.
pros: Free plan with a monthly quota: 10K credits a month at no cost, per the pricing page.
Hebrew speech in the Eleven v3 model: the official languages page lists Hebrew among the 70+ languages of Eleven v3.
Commercial license and voice cloning on the cheap plan: Starter, at 6 USD/month, includes a commercial license and Instant Voice Cloning. Professional cloning starts at Creator.
cons: No commercial license on the free plan: the pricing page lists 'Commercial License' only from Starter up.
Hebrew in only one model: per the languages page, Multilingual v2 and Flash v2.5 don't include Hebrew, so it is only in Eleven v3.
Annual prices not shown: the page has an annual-billing toggle, but annual prices didn't appear in the content read.
elevenlabs.price: Starter is 6 USD/month billed monthly (first month 1 USD in a promotion). Free plan with 10K credits a month.
elevenlabs.free: Free plan: 10K credits a month. The pricing page lists no commercial license on it.
plans: 10K credits/month.
30K credits/month, commercial license, Instant Voice Cloning.
121K credits/month, professional voice cloning.
600K credits/month, 44.1kHz PCM output via API, 192kbps audio.
1.8M credits/month, 3 professional voice clones.
elevenlabs.privacy: Per the help center, ElevenLabs uses some data users provide to improve its audio models. You can opt out in settings (Terms and privacy, then Data use, turn off 'Improve the models for everyone'). By default there is no training on Enterprise customer data. The page doesn't distinguish free from paid plans.
elevenlabs.rights: Per the pricing page, a commercial license is included from Starter up; none is listed on Free. A commercial license doesn't guarantee protection from copyright claims.
elevenlabs.api: Yes. The pricing page mentions 44.1kHz PCM output via API on Pro, and low-latency TTS 'as low as 5c/minute' on Business. A startup grants program offers 12 months free and 33 million characters.
elevenlabs.hebrew: Per the languages page, Hebrew (he) is supported in text-to-speech in the Eleven v3 model, which supports 70+ languages. It isn't in the lists for Multilingual v2 and Flash v2.5. The page doesn't address transcription (Scribe), music or dubbing.
elevenlabs.watch: Users report billing that continued after cancelling and lost credits.

moises.role: App for musicians for stem separation, chord detection and lyrics transcription for practice.
moises.audience: Musicians practicing songs, music teachers and creators who need to separate tracks from a recording.
pros: Basic separation even on free: per the help center, a Free account separates vocals, drums, bass and other instruments. The free plan limits uploads each month.
Long files on Premium: per the help center, Premium includes unlimited uploads under the terms of use, and separation of files up to 20 minutes.
Professional tools on Pro: Pro adds 48kHz/24-bit WAV export, dialogue, effects and soundtrack separation, drum-part separation and Voice Studio for changing voice timbre.
cons: Prices shown only after login: the public pricing page points to a table at studio.moises.ai that opens only after sign-in, and the help pages on Premium and Pro give no price.
Unlimited uploads only when paid: per the FAQ, full functionality and unlimited uploads need a paid subscription.
Some tools are Pro-only: per the help center, Multimedia Tracks separation and drum-part separation are only on Pro.
moises.free: Per the pricing-page FAQ: a limited number of uploads each month and a selection of features. Amount not stated.
plans: Limited uploads per month, separation of vocals, drums, bass and other instruments.
Unlimited uploads under the terms of use, separation of files up to 20 minutes. Price not verified.
48kHz/24-bit WAV export, processing priority, Hi-Fi models, Multimedia Tracks, drum-part separation, Voice Studio, VST plugin with 8 channels. Price not verified.
moises.privacy: Per the official FAQ, 'Moises will never train on your data', and models are trained only on licensed material. The privacy policy (updated 8 June 2026) says Moises accesses only files the user chose to upload.
moises.rights: Per the help center, Moises doesn't claim ownership of outputs and the user keeps ownership of files they uploaded. Outputs may be used 'including commercially', provided the user has the rights.

speechify.role: App that reads texts, documents and web pages aloud in synthetic voices.
speechify.audience: Students and readers who want to listen to reading material, including people with dyslexia or reading difficulties.
pros: Free read-aloud with no stated quota: the free plan includes reading at up to 1.5x speed and 10 voices, with no usage limit on the pricing page.
400+ voices and 60+ languages on Premium: Premium includes natural voices, reading up to 5x, scan-and-read of photographed text and AI summaries.
Connects to storage services: Premium connects to Google Drive, Dropbox and Microsoft OneDrive.
cons: Free voices are robotic: per the page, Free includes '10 robotic sounding voices' and 'Text to speech features only'.
Premium is pricey monthly: 29 USD/month billed monthly, versus 139 USD/year billed annually.
Read-aloud is not for commercial use: per the terms, only narration from Speechify Voice Over Studio may be used commercially. Studio is priced on a separate page that wasn't read.
speechify.price: Premium is 29 USD/month billed monthly, or 139 USD/year. Free plan with 10 basic voices.
speechify.free: Free plan: reading up to 1.5x speed and 10 robotic voices, text-to-speech only.
plans: Reading up to 1.5x speed, 10 robotic voices, text-to-speech only.
400+ voices, 60+ languages, reading up to 5x, scan and read, AI summaries and chat, voice typing, AI Podcasts.
Same as monthly Premium.
speechify.privacy: Not verified. The terms don't explicitly mention model training, but allow Speechify to use user content 'for our internal business purposes' and grant it a broad license to use it. Privacy policy not read.
speechify.rights: Per the terms (updated 1 July 2025), the services 'are not intended for your commercial use', except Speechify Voice Over Studio, where AI narration may be used commercially.
speechify.api: Yes. The pricing page points to a separate Speechify API pricing page, which wasn't read.
speechify.hebrew: Per a 2022 Speechify blog post (old source), 'Speechify can assist with your Hebrew TTS needs', in read-aloud in mobile apps and browser extensions. The post doesn't mention Hebrew in Speechify Studio.
speechify.students: The pricing page states no student price. It links to Education and Speechify for Enterprise & EDU pages, which weren't read.
speechify.watch: Users report unexpected subscription renewals and charges, and difficulty getting a refund.

udio.role: Tool for creating songs and music from a text description, now operating under temporary transition terms.
udio.audience: Those who want to try AI song creation and listen on the site, while downloads are disabled.
udio.status: Active. Per the official blog (19 Nov 2025), Udio operates under temporary transition terms of service effective 12 November while it builds a new platform with record labels. No launch date for the new platform was published. Per the blog, the labels did not acquire Udio. Per the help center, downloading audio, video and stems is disabled. The official blog has no post newer than 19 Nov 2025.
pros: Free renewing credits: a free account has 10 credits a day, then an additional monthly quota of 100 credits. Quotas reset at the start of each month.
Higher quotas on paid plans: Standard allows up to 2,400 credits a month and Pro up to 6,000. Separately purchased credits don't expire.
Existing models remain available during the transition: per the blog, models v1, v1.5 and v1.5 Allegro keep working during the move to the new platform.
cons: You can't download the songs: per the help center, downloading audio, video and stems is disabled. The source doesn't say if this is permanent.
Service runs under temporary transition terms: they apply since 12 November, and the announced new platform still has no date. The terms themselves weren't read.
Monthly credits don't accumulate: unused credits don't roll over. On cancelling, the account returns to free quotas.
udio.price: Free plan with 10 credits a day plus 100 a month. Standard and Pro prices not verified.
udio.free: Free account with 10 credits a day and an additional monthly quota of 100 credits, reset at the start of each month.
udio.trial: The help center mentions a trial that doesn't increase quotas and is limited to 3 songs a day. Length not stated.
plans: 10 credits/day, plus a monthly quota of 100 credits.
Up to 2,400 credits/month. Price not verified.
Up to 6,000 credits/month, five song series in parallel. Price not verified.
udio.rights: Per a help article of 26 Mar 2025, Udio doesn't claim ownership of content and the user owns the output. Free users must state that Udio made the song; paid subscribers get fuller rights while subscribed.
udio.watch: Users report they can't download the songs they created.

murf.role: Voiceover generator that converts text to speech in AI voices, for videos, presentations and training.
murf.audience: Creators of training videos, presentations and marketing content who need narration.
pros: Free trial with no credit card: per the help center, the free trial includes 10 minutes of voice generation and 10 minutes of transcription, no credit card.
Choice of voices and languages: per the help center, the trial gives access to 300+ voices in 33 languages.
Commercial rights on every paid plan: per the help center, all paid plans include commercial rights in narration. Broadcasting rights are reserved for Enterprise.
cons: No file downloads in the free trial: per the help center, 'The free trial does not support downloads'. You can only share a preview or embed link.
Prices not verified: the pricing page renders only with JavaScript and wasn't read.
murf.trial: Automatic free trial for new users: 10 minutes of voice generation and 10 minutes of transcription, 300+ voices in 33 languages, no downloads and no credit card.
murf.rights: Per the help center, all paid plans include commercial rights in narration generated in Studio. A Business License is recommended for registered businesses and organizations, and broadcasting rights are for Enterprise.
murf.api: Yes. Per the product updates page, Murf's API includes the Falcon model at 0.01 USD per 1,000 characters (update of 10 Nov 2025), and from Sept 2026 instant voice cloning for Enterprise customers.
murf.hebrew: Not mentioned in source: the language and accent list in the help center (42 items, though the page says 33 languages) doesn't include Hebrew.
murf.students: An official page for Educators, Students & Non-Profits exists but wasn't read, so the benefit amount and terms weren't verified.

adobe-podcast.role: Browser tool for cleaning and enhancing speech recordings, remote recording and podcast editing.
adobe-podcast.audience: Podcast creators, students and video creators who record speech in non-ideal conditions.
adobe-podcast.status: Active. Per the plans page, Adobe Podcast Premium is offered as part of the Adobe Firefly Pro plan. The date of the change wasn't verified.
pros: Speech cleanup in any language: per the FAQ, Enhance Speech 'is language agnostic': it improves a recording without translating or generating speech.
Cleanup up to 4 hours a day on Premium: Enhance Speech on Premium processes up to 4 hours a day, files up to 1GB, also MP4 and MOV video, with bulk upload.
Separate tuning of speech, music and background: in Premium you can adjust each separately so the result sounds natural.
cons: Premium access moved to Firefly Pro: the plans page shows Adobe Podcast Premium only as part of Firefly Pro, at 19.99 USD/month regular price, with Firefly generation credits.
Daily limits on free use: per the FAQ there are daily limits by plan, but amounts aren't detailed.
Browser tool only: per the FAQ it is web-based, and recording and editing happen in the browser. No app is mentioned.
adobe-podcast.price: Adobe Podcast Premium is included in Firefly Pro, regular price 19.99 USD/month. Free use also exists with daily limits.
adobe-podcast.free: Free use of browser tools with daily limits. Amounts not stated on the pages read.
adobe-podcast.trial: The page has a 'Start free trial' button without trial length or the price after it.
plans: Use of Enhance Speech and browser tools, with daily limits.
Enhance Speech up to 4 hours a day and files up to 1GB, unlimited downloads in Studio, download of original recordings per speaker, 4,000 Firefly generation credits/month.
adobe-podcast.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. Per the FAQ Enhance Speech 'is language agnostic' and doesn't generate or translate speech, but the page lists no supported languages.
adobe-podcast.students: No Firefly student discount found: the Students & Teachers tab on the Firefly page shows the same prices. The student discount in the site menu concerns Creative Cloud, and whether it covers Podcast Premium wasn't checked.

lalal-ai.role: Tool for separating vocals, instruments and noise from audio and video files into separate stems.
lalal-ai.audience: Musicians, DJs, video editors and podcast creators who need to isolate vocals, an instrument or speech from a recording.
pros: Separation into many instrument types: per the site you can extract vocals, accompaniment, drums, bass, guitar, synthesizer, strings and wind instruments.
Cheap subscription: Lite is 7.50 USD/month (90 USD billed annually), with 90 minutes in the fast queue and an unlimited regular queue.
Files aren't used for training: per the privacy policy, LALAL.AI doesn't use user files for AI training.
cons: Free plan is for testing only: Starter includes 10 minutes in the regular queue and files up to 200MB. Per the page it is 'best for testing the service'.
Each separation type is counted separately: minutes used are file length times the number of separation types.
No refund: per the page, 'The subscription is non-refundable'.
lalal-ai.price: Lite is 90 USD/year (7.50 USD/month) billed annually. Free plan with 10 processing minutes.
lalal-ai.free: Free Starter plan: 10 processing minutes in the regular queue and files up to 200MB. The page doesn't say whether minutes renew.
plans: 10 minutes in the regular queue, files up to 200MB.
Unlimited regular queue, 90 minutes/month in the fast queue, files up to 2GB, one voice pack.
Unlimited regular queue, 250 minutes/month in the fast queue, files up to 2GB, 3 voice packs, VST plugin, API.
750 fast-queue minutes, one-time purchase.
3,000 fast-queue minutes, one-time purchase.
lalal-ai.privacy: Per the privacy policy (updated 30 July 2026), the company 'does not use user files for artificial intelligence training or other content'. No retention period for uploaded or processed files is stated, only that personal data is kept as long as needed and deleted per statutory retention periods. You can request deletion by email to support.
lalal-ai.rights: Not verified. The terms of service (updated 30 July 2026) don't say who owns the separated stems and don't address commercial use of them. The user is 'solely responsible' for rights in uploaded material.
lalal-ai.api: Yes. Per the pricing page, API access is included in the Pro plan.
lalal-ai.hebrew: Not mentioned in source: the site's language selector has 12 languages and Hebrew isn't among them.
lalal-ai.students: The pricing page mentions no student benefit.

stable-audio.role: Stability AI's music and sound-effects generator from text and audio.
stable-audio.audience: Video creators, game developers and musicians who need background music, loops or effects.
pros: Long songs with Stable Audio 3.0: per Stability AI, outputs reach 6 minutes 20 seconds, with length control down to the second.
Ownership of the audio and commercial use: per Stability AI, generated audio belongs to the user and may be distributed and commercialized.
Purchased credits don't expire: per the knowledge base, separately purchased credit packs 'never expire'.
cons: No renewing free plan: a new account gets 50 one-time credits for trying. The knowledge base shows no free plan.
Subscription credits don't accumulate: they renew each billing cycle and don't roll over.
stable-audio.price: Per Stability AI's knowledge base: Creator is 12 USD/month. A new account gets 50 one-time credits.
stable-audio.trial: 50 one-time credits for each new account, for trying.
plans: 660 credits/month.
1,800 credits/month.
6,000 credits/month.
14,000 credits/month.
stable-audio.privacy: Not verified. Per Stability AI, all Stable Audio 3.0 models were trained 'on fully licensed data'. The pages read don't address using users' prompts or creations for training.
stable-audio.rights: Per Stability AI, "you own the audio you generate and can distribute and commercialize it". For open-source models: a free Community license for commercial use by organizations under a revenue threshold.

google-flow-music.role: Studio for creating music and songs with a Google AI agent based on the Lyria model.
google-flow-music.audience: Creators and musicians who want to write and produce songs in conversation with an AI agent.
google-flow-music.status: Active. ProducerAI joined Google Labs and now operates as Google Flow Music. Google's blog describes it as a joining, not an acquisition. A separate product from Google Flow for video: it has its own site and pricing page at flowmusic.app.
pros: Free daily credits: the free plan renews daily credits and allows 2 parallel generations, with all core capabilities.
Relatively cheap subscription for many songs: Starter at 6 USD/month includes 3,000 credits, about 600 songs per the page, plus daily credits.
Lyria 3.5 model: per Google, the version released 29 July 2026 improves lyrics, vocals and pronunciation, and adds control of tempo and length.
cons: SynthID watermark on all outputs: per Google's blog, all outputs carry SynthID, Google's watermark for identifying AI-generated content.
Commercial-use rights not detailed: the pricing page and blog posts read don't address song ownership or commercial use.
google-flow-music.price: Starter is 8 USD/month billed monthly, or 6 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with daily credits.
google-flow-music.free: Free plan with no cost and no credit card, for ages 18+ in supported regions: daily credits (amount not stated), 2 parallel generations and all core capabilities.
plans: Daily credits only, 2 parallel generations, all core capabilities.
3,000 credits/month (about 600 songs) plus daily credits, 8 parallel generations.
Same as monthly Starter.
10,000 credits/month (about 2,000 songs) plus daily credits, 12 parallel generations.
Same as monthly Plus.
30,000 credits/month (about 6,000 songs) plus daily credits, 16 parallel generations, early access to new features, events and merchandise for members.
Same as monthly Member.
google-flow-music.rights: Per the pricing-page FAQ, use is subject to Google's terms of use and Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy. Google doesn't claim ownership of original content the user creates.
google-flow-music.watermark: Per Google, all outputs carry SynthID.
